label: Nursing student
values: No shortcuts on the ones that count
mission: Finish strong, pass NCLEX on the first attempt, and start this career without the debt and the fear running the show.
sub: Amara Osei, SN · final-semester BSN · 240 clinical hours to go · NCLEX in the spring · working weekends to stay afloat.
seasonBody: Everything is subordinate to graduating and passing. You wrote that down in March precisely so that saying no in October would be easier.
seasonMeta: Week 9 of 15 · 240 clinical hours remaining · NCLEX window opens 12 March

actions.title: Do the 25 questions you skipped on Tuesday
actions.why: Reading rationales is where your score actually moves, and Scholar queued these from your own misses rather than a generic bank.

actions.title: Certify your aid paperwork before the 31st
actions.why: Dated, and missing it costs a semester of eligibility. This is the single highest-consequence form on your list and it takes minutes.
actions.cost: 15 minutes · waits at a human gate

actions.title: Put one full day off on the calendar
actions.why: You have worked or been in clinical eleven days straight. Nobody passes NCLEX on a deficit, and the calendar is the only place this becomes real.

health.signal: Eleven days straight between shifts and clinical rotations.
health.detail: You are the only person who can protect this one. Florence will not schedule around it for you — but she will keep showing you the count until it changes.

family.signal: Sunday calls home held six weeks running.
family.detail: The one thing you have not let the semester take. It costs forty minutes and it is doing more than you think.

career.signal: Two residency applications drafted. One reference secured, one asked.
career.detail: New-grad residency deadlines cluster in January. Your second reference has been pending three weeks — a nudge is not a burden to the person who offered.

learning.signal: NCLEX readiness 58% and climbing. Pharm and prioritization are the gaps.
learning.detail: Your practice scores have risen every fortnight since August. Prioritization questions are where you lose the most, and they are the most teachable.

finance.signal: Aid certification due 31 August. Two scholarship deadlines in October.
finance.detail: Money is taking a large share of your attention because it is unresolved, not because you are careless. Three dated forms would take most of this off the board.

creative.signal: Four study aids you made yourself; two classmates now use them.
creative.detail: You have quietly built teaching materials all semester. That is a portfolio, not a study habit.

service.signal: Peer tutoring twice a week since September.
service.detail: Teaching is the reason your own retention is climbing. The tutoring is study time, and it should be counted as such.

business.signal: Weekend job held at 16 hours — capped by you until NCLEX.
business.detail: You set the cap in March and have not broken it once. Holding a line under pressure is the whole skill, and you already have it.

momentum.label: returned to you this month — mostly study planning, references, and paperwork you no longer redo from scratch.
momentum.note: Estimated from your own logged times. It is deliberately conservative: only tasks you timed both before and after.
momentum.caption: the habit stuck in week 4

risks.what: A clinical story told with too much detail
risks.guard: Import refuses on PHI indicators and a nightly lint sweeps what is already stored. The system catches it.

risks.what: AI-written work submitted as your own
risks.guard: Your program’s integrity policy governs this, and no software can enforce it for you. NAIO drafts, coaches, and quizzes; it never submits. This one is yours to keep — and it is the one that ends careers before they start.

risks.what: Reaching for an ungoverned window instead
risks.guard: No governed system can reach a chat window it does not run. This one is yours to keep — it is the reason the rails are worth having.

license.scopeNote: You do not have a license yet. That is exactly why this panel exists. Everything here is the habit that will protect the license you are about to earn — the boundary you keep now is the one you will still be keeping at year eleven.

signals.title: Aid certification is due on 31 August
signals.body: The highest-consequence item on your board, and it takes fifteen minutes. Nothing else here has a cliff behind it.

signals.title: Your second reference has waited three weeks
signals.body: She offered. Following up is not a burden — it is the part of the ask you have not finished.

signals.title: Prioritization is your widest NCLEX gap
signals.body: It is also the most teachable one, and it responds fastest to rationale reading.

signals.title: Eleven days worked or in clinical, straight
signals.body: Noticed, not judged. One full day off is the cheapest intervention available to you right now.

opps.title: New-grad residency applications open
opps.body: Cardiac and ICU tracks both open in January; two of your rotations map directly.

opps.title: Two deadlines you already qualify for
opps.body: Both need an essay you have effectively already written across your reflections.

opps.title: Your Tuesday preceptor offered a reference
opps.body: Unprompted, six weeks ago. Your notes say you meant to take her up on it.

opps.title: Your study aids are good enough to share
opps.body: Two classmates already use them. Sanitized, they would help a whole cohort.

agents.name: Florence
agents.scope: All spheres, read-only outside Health. Drafts freely; sends nothing.

agents.name: Scholar
agents.scope: Learning sphere only. Builds sets from your misses; never writes graded work.

agents.name: Scribe
agents.scope: Career and Finance spheres. No outbound send, ever.
agents.await: Drafted your clinical reflection — your program requires your own words
